name: Aminata Diallo
action: Aminata pauses, then gives Sékou a quiet, respectful refusal: "Thank you, Sékou. Please greet your wife for me, but I have to go back and study tonight."
reason: Her initial tendency was to hesitate and answer carefully, balancing politeness against the pull of the meal, her money, and her study time. Reflection softened that impulse by making the Korité invitation feel more meaningful and by recalling her mother’s holiday-meal memory, but it also made the practical cost of bus fare and lost study time feel heavier. Because Aminata is habitually restrained, private, and protective of her exam preparation and limited resources, the revised tendency to decline unless she could do so without giving up much leads to a courteous refusal rather than an impulsive acceptance. The remaining conflict is that she still wants to honor Sékou’s family invitation, so she refuses gently and acknowledges the welcome instead of sounding abrupt.
